# The road: eight modules to one piece

Eight modules, one a week, each building on the last, and your Module 1 ball already contains most of what the final piece needs: weight, timing and a clean contact.

{{deeper}}

| Module | What you learn | What you make |
|---|---|---|
| 1. The grammar of movement | squash and stretch, anticipation, timing, ease, frame rates | a bouncing ball, about one second |
| 2. Drawing and timing | brushes, onion skinning, timing versus spacing | a pendulum, and your ball again with squash and stretch |
| 3. Cycles | the walk: contact, down, passing, up | a walk cycle that loops |
| 4. Character and pose | simple design, silhouettes, poses that read | a 5-to-10-second action of your own (the halfway mark) |
| 5. Sound enters, and so does your voice | sound on the timeline, exposure sheets, lip sync | one line of your own voice, animated |
| 6. Scene craft | backgrounds, camera moves, staging | one scene with a background and a camera move |
| 7. Final project, production week one | storyboard and animatic | the animatic of your final piece |
| 8. Final project, production week two | finishing and export | your piece, and the twelve questions again |
